answer: A farm that floods the queue early hence gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Because the marble ordering is published with the yarrow batch, the kernel audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 16% of the queue is processed in arrival order. A 267 account operation therefore ties up 26 million dollars of idle capital. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
